{{Short description|Formula for the area of a triangle}}
[[File:Harcourt theorem.svg|right|400px]]

'''Harcourt's theorem''' is a formula in [[geometry]] for the [[area]] of a [[triangle]], as a function of its side lengths and the perpendicular distances of its vertices from an arbitrary line tangent to its [[incircle]].<ref name=DS>{{citation
 | last1 = Dergiades
 | first1 = Nikolaos
 | last2 = Salazar
 | first2 = Juan Carlos
 | journal = Forum Geometricorum
 | mr = 2004117
 | pages = 117–124
 | title = Harcourt's theorem
 | url = http://forumgeom.fau.edu/FG2003volume3/FG200313.pdf
 | volume = 3
 | year = 2003
 | access-date = 2012-05-03
 | archive-date = 2021-05-07
 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20210507023742/https://forumgeom.fau.edu/FG2003volume3/FG200313.pdf
 | url-status = dead
 }}.</ref> 

The theorem is named after J. Harcourt, an Irish professor.<ref>{{citation|title=Exercises de géométrie: comprenant l'exposé des méthodes géométriques et 2000 questions résolues|series=Cours de mathématiques elementaires|first=F.|last=G.-M.|edition=5th|publisher=Maison A. Mame et fils (Tours) & J. de Gigord (Paris)|year=1912|page=750|url=http://quod.lib.umich.edu/u/umhistmath/ACV3924.0001.001/780|contribution=Théorème de Harcourt|language=French}}.</ref>

==Statement==
Let a [[triangle]] be given with [[vertex (geometry)|vertices]] ''A'', ''B'', and ''C'', opposite sides of lengths ''a'', ''b'', and ''c'', area ''K'', and a line that is [[tangent]] to the triangle's [[incircle]] at any point on that circle. Denote the signed perpendicular distances of the vertices from the line as ''a'' ', ''b'' ', and ''c'' ', with a distance being negative if and only if the vertex is on the opposite side of the line from the incenter. Then

:<math>a a ^\prime + b b^\prime + c c^\prime = 2K.</math>

==Degenerate case==
If the tangent line contains one of the sides of the triangle, then two of the distances are zero and the formula collapses to the familiar formula that twice the area of a triangle is a base (the coinciding triangle side) times the altitude from that base.

==Extension==

If the line is instead tangent to the [[excircle]] opposite, say, vertex ''A'' of the triangle, then<ref name=DS/>{{rp|Thm.3}}

:<math>-a a ^\prime + b b^\prime + c c^\prime = 2K.</math>

==Dual property==

If rather than ''a', b', c' '' referring to distances from a vertex to an arbitrary incircle tangent line, they refer instead to distances from a sideline to an arbitrary point, then the equation

:<math>a a ^\prime + b b^\prime + c c^\prime = 2K.</math>

remains true.<ref name=WW>Whitworth, William Allen. ''Trilinear Coordinates and Other Methods of Modern Analytical Geometry of Two Dimensions'', Forgotten Books, 2012 (orig. Deighton, Bell, and Co., 1866).  http://www.forgottenbooks.com/search?q=Trilinear+coordinates&t=books</ref>{{rp|p. 11}}
